title: Reconstruct Transcendence as exact HC base plus overlay
claim: Where Transcendence duplicates HC Brain implementation, exact base-plus-overlay reconstruction may preserve Transcendence-specific research while eliminating copied base maintenance.
preserved_boundaries: Transcendence-specific BCI, continuity, and experimental material remains independently owned.
No duplicated file is removed until exact reconstruction is demonstrated.
rejection_conditions: An exact historical/candidate Transcendence tree cannot be reconstructed from a pinned HC base plus overlay.
The overlay would inherit HC assumptions that Transcendence must be able to modify independently.
The dependency materially increases failure or migration risk.

critical_objections: Copied code may be intentional experimental isolation rather than accidental duplication.
A base dependency can silently constrain future divergent research.

notes: Measure exact byte-identical overlap again at experiment time; do not carry old counts forward as current truth.
